When a matchup is absent from the live roster, the engine's probabilistic models lack observational targets, leading to a null posterior. This results in 'fiction analysis'—unverifiable statements that violate epistemic standards. To prevent this, the system enforces a veto condition: cards are only generated when the matchup is confirmed on the slate. If the matchup is missing, the engine refuses to produce analysis, preventing the propagation of false narratives. Instead, users must re-run the query with the correct opponent names from the actual games played that week, allowing the system to compute valid posterior distributions and define sensible state transitions.
